metadata.methodology: Symptoms extracted only when explicitly mentioned by at least 2 authoritative medical sources. Synonyms normalized. False negatives preferred over false positives.

diseases.description: A chronic respiratory condition in which the airways narrow and swell, producing extra mucus, making breathing difficult and triggering coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath.
diseases.etiology: Chronic inflammatory airway disease; triggered by allergens, exercise, cold air, irritants

diseases.description: A group of progressive lung diseases, including emphysema and chronic bronchitis, that cause airflow obstruction and breathing-related problems.
diseases.etiology: Long-term exposure to irritating gases or particulate matter, most often from cigarette smoke

diseases.description: A short-term inflammation of the bronchial tubes, usually caused by a viral infection, resulting in coughing and mucus production.
diseases.etiology: Most commonly viral (rhinovirus, influenza, RSV); occasionally bacterial

diseases.description: A common lower respiratory tract infection in infants and young children, usually caused by RSV, causing inflammation and congestion in the small airways.
diseases.etiology: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) most common; also human metapneumovirus, rhinovirus

diseases.description: Inflammation or swelling of the tissue lining the sinuses, leading to blocked sinuses filled with fluid, often following a cold.
diseases.etiology: Viral (most common), bacterial, allergic, or fungal

diseases.description: Inflammation of the pharynx (back of the throat), causing a sore throat. Most often viral, but bacterial pharyngitis (strep throat) requires antibiotic treatment.
diseases.etiology: Viral (rhinovirus, adenovirus, EBV most common); bacterial (Group A Streptococcus)

diseases.description: Inflammation of the larynx (voice box), usually from overuse, irritation, or infection, causing hoarseness or loss of voice.

symptoms.symptom: tickling sensation or rawness in throat

diseases.etiology: Viral infection (most common), vocal strain, bacterial infection (rare)

diseases.description: Inflammation of the pleura (the double-layered membrane surrounding the lungs), causing sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing.

symptoms.symptom: sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing
pain worsened by coughing or sneezing

diseases.etiology: Viral infection (most common), bacterial infection, pulmonary embolism, autoimmune conditions

diseases.description: A blockage in one of the pulmonary arteries in the lungs, usually caused by blood clots that travel from the legs (deep vein thrombosis).
diseases.etiology: Blood clot (thrombus) from deep vein thrombosis (DVT)

diseases.description: A group of disorders characterized by progressive scarring (fibrosis) of the lung tissue, affecting the ability to breathe and get enough oxygen into the bloodstream.
diseases.etiology: Various causes including occupational exposures, autoimmune diseases, medications; often idiopathic (IPF)

diseases.description: A potentially serious sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep due to throat muscles relaxing and blocking the airway.

symptoms.symptom: episodes of stopped breathing during sleep
dry mouth or sore throat upon awakening

diseases.etiology: Upper airway collapse during sleep

diseases.description: A long-term condition where the airways of the lungs become abnormally widened, leading to a build-up of excess mucus that can make the lungs more vulnerable to infection.

symptoms.symptom: coughing up large amounts of mucus/sputum

diseases.etiology: Chronic airway inflammation/infection, often due to cystic fibrosis, prior severe lung infections, or immune deficiencies

diseases.description: A type of high blood pressure that specifically affects the arteries in the lungs and the right side of the heart.

symptoms.symptom: swelling in ankles, legs, or abdomen
bluish color to lips or skin

diseases.etiology: Idiopathic, genetic, left-sided heart disease, chronic lung disease, or chronic blood clots

diseases.description: A collapsed lung that occurs when air leaks into the space between the lung and the chest wall, pushing on the outside of the lung and making it collapse.
diseases.etiology: Chest injury, lung disease, ruptured air blisters (blebs), or mechanical ventilation

diseases.description: An unusual build-up of fluid in the pleural space between the lungs and the chest wall, often called 'water on the lungs.'
diseases.etiology: Heart failure, pneumonia, cancer, pulmonary embolism, liver or kidney disease

diseases.description: A collection of pus in the pleural cavity, the space between the lungs and the inner surface of the chest wall, usually caused by a bacterial infection like pneumonia.
diseases.etiology: Bacterial infection spreading from the lungs (pneumonia), chest trauma, or chest surgery

diseases.description: A lung disease that occurs when lung tissue becomes damaged and scarred, making it difficult for the lungs to work properly.
diseases.etiology: Idiopathic (IPF), environmental/occupational exposure, medications, radiation, autoimmune disorders

diseases.description: A disease characterized by the growth of tiny collections of inflammatory cells (granulomas) in any part of the body, most commonly the lungs and lymph nodes.

symptoms.symptom: tender red bumps on skin (erythema nodosum)

diseases.etiology: Unknown immune system reaction, possibly triggered by infections, chemicals, or dust

diseases.description: An inherited disorder that causes severe damage to the lungs, digestive system, and other organs by producing thick, sticky mucus.
diseases.etiology: Genetic mutation in the CFTR gene

diseases.description: A type of lung infection that develops after inhaling food, liquid, vomit, or saliva into the lungs.
diseases.etiology: Inhalation of foreign material into the lungs, often due to impaired swallowing or gag reflex

diseases.description: A rapidly progressive, life-threatening condition in which fluid leaks into the lungs, making breathing difficult or impossible.
diseases.etiology: Severe injury or illness, such as sepsis, pneumonia, major trauma, or inhaling harmful substances

diseases.description: A broad group of lung diseases caused by inhaling irritating or toxic substances in the workplace over a long period.
diseases.etiology: Inhalation of dusts, chemicals, gases, or fumes at work

diseases.description: An inflammation of the lungs caused by breathing in a foreign substance, such as certain dusts, fungus, or molds, leading to an allergic reaction.
diseases.etiology: Allergic reaction to inhaled organic dusts (e.g., bird droppings, moldy hay)

diseases.description: A long-term lung disease caused by inhaling large amounts of crystalline silica dust, leading to inflammation and scarring in the lungs.
diseases.etiology: Prolonged inhalation of silica dust

diseases.description: A chronic lung disease caused by inhaling asbestos fibers, resulting in lung tissue scarring and shortness of breath.
diseases.etiology: Prolonged inhalation of asbestos fibers
